A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with the same authors, title, core method, and appendices A–F. Their text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support reliable comparison, including relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SMC benchmark experiments, dimensional-scaling results, backward-kernel comparisons, and adaptation diagnostics in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional results for the Downloads benchmark.

M1.justification: The incremental-KL objective, particle subsampling, fixed randomness, regularization, step-size search, and KLMC coordinate updates are retained. v2's Algorithm 4 formalizes the schedule-adaptation workflow already described in v1 Appendix B.1. Index corrections do not establish a changed underlying procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds Downloads, a 62-dimensional Prophet model of rstan download counts, to the benchmark comparisons and diagnostics. Existing coverage is retained. The Three Men description changes from corpus 2 to corpus 3, but both versions already identify the dataset as three_men3, supporting a documentation correction.

E2.justification: The fixed-parameter kernels, differentiable AIS variants with and without variational reference tuning, and MALA-ESJD/MALA-ARC comparators are retained. Figures 15 and 17 correct duplicated legend labels to identify the existing VI comparator. Figure 11 claims an omission but still displays the VI curve; this does not establish removal of an evaluated method.

E3.justification: The stated particle budgets, annealing settings, optimizer iterations and learning rates, model configurations, and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Sonar's intercept is newly disclosed rather than established as a changed setting. Changes to plotted axis ranges alone do not establish revised experimental budgets.

E4.justification: Appendices F.3–F.4 extend objective-evaluation cost and learned-schedule diagnostics to Downloads and update displayed adaptation trajectories for retained problems. These are limited extensions of existing analyses. The backward-kernel ablation and dimensional-scaling study were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report 32 replications and 80% empirical quantiles for benchmark comparisons, 256 replications for the backward-kernel study, and eight selected trajectories in Appendix F.4. No new repeated-run, significance-testing, or uncertainty-reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds Downloads results, changes the Section 5.2 summary from 20 of 21 to 20 of 22 benchmarks, and updates plotted estimates and trajectories in Appendix F.4. Figure 11 newly reports divergence for Brownian VI tuning at learning rate 10^-2, although its claimed omission conflicts with the retained curve. The broad comparative findings remain stable.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 revises Corollary 1 from a warm-start-specific statement to a general unimodal guarantee, retaining the warm-start bound as a consequence. The parameter guidance changes from cr = O(1/epsilon) to c/r = O(epsilon). Appendix B.1 also corrects the cumulative communication-barrier summation index; the main appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: incremental-KL adaptation, gradient- and tuning-free step-size optimization, LMC/KLMC implementations, and inexpensive tuning with competitive estimates. The revised benchmark count changes supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 qualifies the objective estimate as conditionally unbiased rather than unbiased. Section 4.2 removes the assertion that the coarse refreshment grid has minimal impact. Figure 11 introduces a specific instability qualification for variational reference tuning, although its accompanying plot is inconsistent with the caption.

D1.justification: The implementation link changes from ControlledSMC.jl v0.0.3 to v0.0.4. Appendix A explicitly documents Sonar's intercept, supplies Downloads model/data identifiers, and corrects the Three Men corpus description. These improve implementation and data documentation without establishing changes to retained experimental settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds Taylor and Letham (2018) and Bales et al. (2019) in connection with Downloads. Its substantive positioning relative to annealed flow transport, adaptive SMC, and differentiable AIS remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify the divergence construction, convergence discussion, KLMC backward kernel, and appendix explanations. Terminology is standardized, and an Impact Statement, funding acknowledgements, and conference information are added. The overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds identifying legends to fixed-step comparisons, corrects VI legend labels, adds Downloads panels, and adjusts axes and subplot placement. Appendix F.2 figures are packed more compactly, and existing schedule-adaptation steps become an algorithm box. These are localized display and layout revisions.

improvement.justification: Corrected parameter-scaling guidance and the cumulative-barrier formula, clearer implementation details, and identifying plot legends modestly improve precision and reproducibility. Downloads provides a limited extension of the evidence. These gains are tempered by Figure 11's new omission claim contradicting its retained VI curve, leaving a reporting inconsistency.
